title: Emergency Management Commissioner

evidence.source_text: A Class 1 emergency is either: a major fire; or any other major emergency for which the control agency is the MFB, CFA or VICSES.

A Class 2 emergency is a major emergency that is not: a Class 1 emergency; or a warlike act or act of terrorism, whether directed at Victoria or at any other state or territory of the Commonwealth; or a hi jack, siege or riot.

nodes.text: Legislated management responsibilities across major emergencies (except security-related)

evidence.source_text: Under the EM Act 2013, the EMC has legislated management responsibilities across major emergencies, with the exception of security-related emergencies.

nodes.text: Ensure effective control arrangements are established

evidence.source_text: ensuring effective control arrangements are established...

nodes.text: Ensure response to emergencies in Victoria is systematic and coordinated

evidence.source_text: The EMC functions include accountability for ensuring the response to emergencies in Victoria is systematic and coordinated.

nodes.text: Power to do all things necessary or convenient for the performance of EMC functions

evidence.source_text: Section 33 of the EM Act 2013 gives the EMC the power to do all things that are necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with, the performance of the functions of the EMC.
